platform_notes: These are point-of-sale accessories, not payment terminals: they run the makers' own firmware (Star, Epson, Brother, Zebra, CAS) and are driven by whichever register or point-of-sale app they are attached to, so sales, refunds and batches are not done on them. Printers are set up with the makers' utilities (Star Quick Setup Utility / Star Windows Software, Epson TM Utility / Web Config, Brother Printer Setting Tool) and scanners with Zebra setup barcodes or 123Scan. Cash drawers have no software and open on a pulse from the receipt printer's DK port.

entries.title: TSP143IV: power does not turn on
steps: Check that the power cable is properly connected to the printer.
Check that the plug is not loose in the power socket and is securely connected.
entries.quote: If the Power LED does not turn on even when the power is turned on, it may mean that the power cable is not properly connected.

entries.title: TSP143IV on wired LAN: Network LED is not lit
steps: Check that the LAN cable is firmly connected at both the printer and the router or hub.
If the Network LED still does not light, try a different LAN cable.
Check that the router or hub is working.
entries.quote: When the Network LED does not light up even if the LAN cable is reconnected, confirm by connecting a different LAN cable.

entries.title: TSP143IV on wired LAN: Network LED is blinking (IP address cannot be obtained)
steps: The printer cannot get an IP address.
If the network uses a DHCP server (usually the router), check that it is available.
entries.quote: The LED display shows "Link down: IP address cannot be obtained". When a DHCP server is provided, check whether it is available.

entries.title: TSP143IV stopped connecting after its network settings were changed
steps: Run "Initialize Communication Settings" on the printer once.
Check the connection again.
entries.quote: initializing the network may make it possible for the printer to connect

entries.title: TSP143IV Web Configuration says "Up to 2 devices can access at the same time. Please reload in 5 seconds."
steps: Turn on JavaScript in the web browser.
Only two PCs, tablets or phones can open the settings page at once; wait more than 5 seconds and try again.
entries.quote: Up to 2 PCs, tablets, or smartphones can access Web Configuration at the same time.

entries.title: TSP143IV Web Configuration page is not displayed correctly
steps: Open the settings page with http:// followed by the printer's IP address, not https://.
entries.quote: When opening Web Configuration, use "http://[Printer IP address]" (non-SSL/TLS communication).

entries.title: TSP143IV Wi-Fi does not work while a LAN cable is plugged in
steps: Unplug the LAN cable from the printer when you want to use wireless LAN.
Wired and wireless cannot be used together, and the wired connection always takes priority.
entries.quote: The wireless LAN and wired LAN cannot be connected at the same time, and the wired LAN takes priority when the LAN cable is connected.

entries.title: TSP143IV: only the UEWB model has Wi-Fi and Bluetooth
steps: Check the model name on the bottom of the printer.
The TSP143IV-UE model does not support wireless LAN or Bluetooth; the TSP143IV-UEWB does.
entries.quote: Wireless LAN communication is not supported when the TSP143IV-UE model is used.

entries.title: TSP143IV wireless LAN trouble: things to check first
steps: Unplug the LAN cable from the printer.
Check that Wi-Fi is turned on on the phone, tablet or PC and that it is on the intended network; try restarting that device.
Check that the network name (SSID) has no characters that cannot be used.
Check that the router or access point is powered, its lights are normal and its cables are not loose or damaged.
Check in the Star app, under Printer Settings then Network Settings, that the printer's wireless function is ON.
If it still fails, contact whoever looks after the network and try restarting the network devices.
entries.quote: If problems in wireless connection cannot be solved even with the check and countermeasures mentioned above, contact your network administrator and try to restart the network devices.

entries.title: Wireless Network Diagnosis: "(Fail)" printed for the SSID
steps: The network name that was entered was not found.
Turn the printer off and on again to clear the wireless settings.
Check the correct SSID and set it up again.
If it still fails, initialize the printer's communication settings and try again.
Check for obstacles or too much distance between the printer and the access point.
entries.quote: The specified SSID (network) was not found.

entries.title: Wireless Network Diagnosis: "(Fail)" printed for the Security Type
steps: The security type set on the printer does not match the access point.
Turn the printer off and on again to clear the wireless settings.
Check the access point's security type (the printer supports NONE, WPA, WPA2, WPA3) and set it up again.
This also prints when no security key was entered in the app: enter the key, restart the printer and set up again.
If it still fails, initialize the communication settings and set up again.
entries.quote: The Security Type that has been set does not match the Security Type of the access point to be connected.

entries.title: Wireless Network Diagnosis: "(Fail)" printed for the Security Key
steps: The Wi-Fi password entered does not match the access point's password.
Turn the printer off and on again to clear the wireless settings.
Check the access point's password and set it up again.
If it still fails, initialize the communication settings and set up again.
entries.quote: The password (Security Key) that has been set does not match the password of the access point to be connected.

entries.title: TSP143IV wireless settings do not clear when the printer is turned off and on
steps: The automatic reset of wireless settings on power-on is not working.
Initialize the printer's communication settings, then set up Wi-Fi again.
entries.quote: The auto reset function that initializes the wireless settings by turning on the power again does not work.

entries.title: Wireless Network Diagnosis: "(Didn't obtain)" printed for IP Address
steps: The settings are right but the printer could not get an IP address; the wireless link may be unstable.
If Signal Strength shows "(Weak)", move the printer or access point, or put them where there are fewer obstacles.
Check the access point for problems such as DHCP being turned off or too many devices connected.
entries.quote: Also, check the access point settings and network environment for problems, such that the DHCP server is disabled or the maximum number of devices that can be connected is exceeded.

entries.title: TSP143IV: settings screen does not appear after scanning the wireless setup QR code
steps: Run a self-print and read the IP Address under "Current IP Parameters Status".
Type that IP address into a web browser such as Chrome or Safari to open the printer settings screen.
entries.quote: Perform Self-Printing, and check the IP Address of "Current IP Parameters Status".

entries.title: TSP143IV: Wi-Fi setup fails when setting up several printers
steps: Turn off every printer except the one being set up.
Set the printers up one at a time.
entries.quote: Turn off all the printers except the one currently undergoing setting, and configure the printers one at a time.

entries.title: TSP143IV on Wi-Fi: lights look normal but nothing prints
steps: Check that the tablet or register and the printer are on the same network; the tablet's network may have changed without anyone noticing.
Check the printing app's settings.
For printer faults such as paper feed trouble, follow the matching fix.
entries.quote: The destination network of the setting devices may be unintentionally changed.

entries.title: TSP143IV Wi-Fi keeps cutting out or is very slow
steps: Move the printer as close to the access point as possible with fewer obstacles between them.
Move the printer away from devices that cause radio interference.
Use a Wi-Fi channel away from the interference.
Use whichever of 2.4 GHz or 5 GHz is less affected.
Changing the printer's location or direction may help.
entries.quote: Install the printer in a place as close to the access point as possible with fewer obstacles.

entries.title: TSP143IV on Wi-Fi: Network LED does not light or blink
steps: The router may be using a Wi-Fi channel the printer does not support.
Change the router's channel to one the printer supports (US model: 2.4 GHz channels 1 to 11).
entries.quote: The destination router uses a channel not supported by the printer.

entries.title: TSP143IV on Wi-Fi: Network LED keeps blinking and never stays lit
steps: The DHCP server may not be working normally.
Check the router settings or the network.
entries.quote: The Network LED continues blinking and does not light up.

entries.title: TSP143IV Wi-Fi signal strength: what the number means
steps: The closer the signal strength is to 0, the better.
At -70 dBm or lower the wireless connection may become unstable.
The figure is printed on the Wireless Network Diagnosis sheet and shown in the Star app.
entries.quote: It becomes the maximum at -30 dBm, and wireless connection may become unstable at -70 dBm or less.

entries.title: TSP143IV: set a static IP address over Wi-Fi
steps: On an iOS or Android device open Star Quick Setup Utility.
Go to Printer Settings, then Network Settings, and set the static IP address there.
entries.quote: Configure the settings from [Printer Settings] - [Network Settings] in Star Quick Setup Utility.

entries.title: TSP143IV Bluetooth drops when the iPad is plugged into the printer
steps: If an iOS device connected by Bluetooth is also plugged into the printer's USB-C port, the Bluetooth connection may be released.
Unplug it from the USB-C port if Bluetooth is the connection in use.
entries.quote: When the iOS device connected via Bluetooth is connected to the printer USB-C port, Bluetooth connection may be released.

entries.title: TSP143IV: cannot establish Bluetooth communication
steps: Confirm the printer is the TSP143IV-UEWB model; the UE model has no Bluetooth.
Check the Power LED is on; if not, check the power cable, AC adapter and socket.
With an iPad or iPhone, the Power LED and the Bluetooth LED should both be blue; if the Bluetooth LED is off, open the device's Bluetooth settings and check it is connected to the printer.
With Android and other devices, the Bluetooth LED only lights while printing; open the device's Bluetooth settings and check pairing is complete.
Check in the Star app, under Printer Settings then Bluetooth Settings, that the wireless function is ON.
entries.quote: The Bluetooth LED only lights up blue when printing or status acquisition is performed via Bluetooth.

entries.title: TSP143IV Bluetooth: printer is already connected to another iPad or iPhone
steps: Check whether the printer is already connected to another iOS device by Bluetooth.
If it is, remove that connection.
Then connect from the device you want to use.
entries.quote: If connected, then remove the connection to the connected iOS device, and then try to connect to the Bluetooth from another host device.

entries.title: TSP143IV Bluetooth: printer cannot be found or paired by a new tablet (New Pairing Permission is OFF)
steps: When New Pairing Permission is OFF, only the tablet already connected can use the printer.
To allow new pairing again, initialize the printer's Bluetooth settings.
entries.quote: To set [New Pairing Permission] to ON (enable), initialize the network settings (Bluetooth).

entries.title: TSP143IV Bluetooth communication is not stable
steps: Check for nearby objects or radio sources that could interfere.
Check the printer is not too far from the tablet or register.
entries.quote: The communication status of the Bluetooth printer will depend on any nearby radio waves, presence of interference, and the environment in which it is installed.

entries.title: TSP143IV: cannot establish USB communication
steps: Check the USB cable is firmly connected to both the printer and the PC, tablet or phone.
If the problem comes back, try another USB cable.
If the cable was plugged in and pulled out straight away, the printer may not recognise it again: turn the printer off and back on.
entries.quote: If the USB cable is connected and then immediately disconnected, the printer may not recognize the USB cable when it is connected again. If this occurs, turn the power off and back on again.

entries.title: TSP143IV: which USB port does what
steps: The USB-A port talks to and powers Android phones and tablets and Star's own USB accessories; other USB devices only get power from it (1.5 A at most).
The USB-C port talks to Windows, Android, Mac and Linux devices and does not support other USB devices.
entries.quote: The USB-C port communicates with Windows, Android, Mac and Linux devices. It does not support connections with other USB devices.

entries.title: TSP143IV does not work with an iPad or iPhone over USB
steps: This printer does not support a USB connection to an iPad, iPhone or iPod touch.
Use a network connection with those devices instead.
entries.quote: This product does not support USB connections with an iPad, iPhone or iPod touch.

entries.title: TSP143IV: blank paper comes out
steps: The paper roll may be loaded the wrong way round.
Check the direction of the roll and reload it correctly.
entries.quote: If blank paper is being ejected, the paper roll may be set in the wrong direction.

entries.title: TSP143IV: printing is faint, or nothing prints on the paper
steps: This is a thermal printer and will not print on ordinary paper.
Faint print can mean the paper does not meet the printer's specification or is old and deteriorated.
Use a thermal paper roll that meets the printer's specification.
entries.quote: As this product is a thermal printer, it will not print on ordinary paper.

entries.title: TSP143IV: faint or uneven print is not an ink problem
steps: The printer uses no ink, ribbon or toner; the only supply is thermal paper.
Faint or uneven print can come from the type of paper roll, the print density setting or a dirty thermal head.
If printed text fades over time, the paper may be old: use a new roll.
entries.quote: If printing is faint or uneven, the cause is not a lack of ink. Possible causes include the type of paper roll, the print density setting, or a dirty thermal head.

entries.title: TSP143IV: receipt does not print and a light is blinking or red
steps: Check the Power LED is on; if not, check the power cable and socket.
If the Power LED is blinking, or an LED is lit or blinking red or purple, look up the LED display to find the printer's status.
entries.quote: If the Power/Error LED is blinking or the LED is lit/blinking in red or purple, refer to the LED lamp display and check the status of the printer.

entries.title: TSP143IV: printer can be heard working but no paper comes out
steps: There may be a paper jam, or the paper may be wrapped around the rubber roller.
Remove the jammed paper following the paper jam steps.
entries.quote: If you can hear the printer operating but the paper is not being ejected, there is a possibility that a paper jam is occurring or the paper is being rolled onto the rubber roller.

entries.title: TSP143IV: self-print works but receipts from the register do not
steps: Run a self-print.
If the self-print is fine, check that the app, software and printer settings are correct.
On a Windows PC or tablet, check the correct printer queue is selected as the output.
entries.quote: When Self-Printing works correctly, check whether the app, software and printer settings are correctly configured.

entries.title: TSP143IV: paper keeps jamming
steps: Do not touch the paper or block the outlet while paper is coming out.
Do not let printed paper pile up at the paper exit.
Check the paper width and thickness meet the printer's specification.
entries.quote: Do not touch the paper or block the outlet while the paper is being discharged.

entries.title: TSP143IV: printer cover does not close
steps: Check the paper roll is 83 mm in diameter or smaller.
Use a roll that meets the printer's specification.
entries.quote: If the printer cover does not close, confirm that the diameter of the paper roll is 83 mm or smaller.

entries.title: TSP143IV: tablet does not charge from the printer
steps: Check the printer's Power LED is on; devices only charge while the printer is on.
Plug the tablet's cable into the USB-A port (marked Android USB-A).
A Windows, Mac or Linux device on the USB-C port is not charged; use the USB-A port to charge.
The USB-A port supplies 1.5 A at most; check that is enough for the tablet.
entries.quote: USB peripherals such as tablets can only be charged while the power of the main unit is on.

entries.title: TSP143IV: check the printer's settings
steps: Use Star Quick Setup Utility to check the settings.
Or run a self-print, which prints them.
entries.quote: You can also check settings using the Self-Printing function.

entries.title: TSP143IV LED flashes for about 5 seconds after a USB device is plugged in
steps: A device that can only be charged, or that does not talk to the printer, was connected to the USB port.
The LED returns to the normal status display by itself.
entries.quote: When a USB device, tablet, etc. that does not communicate with the printer is connected, the LED flashes for about 5 seconds and then returns to the status display.

entries.title: TSP143IV LED: USB hub connection
steps: A USB hub was connected to the USB-A port; a USB hub cannot be used.
Remove the hub and plug the device straight into the printer.
entries.quote: A USB hub is connected to the USB-A port. (A USB hub cannot be used.)
entries.note: The source says a hub cannot be used; removing it is the implied action.

entries.title: TSP143IV LED: printing stopped, high temperature detected for the head
steps: The print head is hot so printing has stopped.
Wait; printing resumes automatically when the head temperature returns to normal.
entries.quote: When the printer head temperature returns to a normal range, printing will resume automatically.

entries.title: TSP143IV LED: printing stopped, high temperature detected for the substrate
steps: The circuit board is hot so printing has stopped.
Wait; printing resumes automatically when the temperature returns to normal.
entries.quote: When the substrate temperature returns to a normal range, printing will resume automatically.

entries.title: TSP143IV LED: cover open error
steps: The printer cover is open.
Set the paper and close the printer cover; the printer returns to ready.
entries.quote: Set the paper, close the printer cover, and it will move to the power-on status.

entries.title: TSP143IV LED: out of paper error
steps: The printer is out of paper.
Load a new roll and close the printer cover; the printer returns to ready.
entries.quote: The printer is out of paper.

entries.title: TSP143IV LED: cutter error
steps: The cutter did not work properly.
Turn the power off.
If paper is jammed, remove it.
Move the cutter's movable part back to its home position following the Cutter Lock steps.
If the same error shows afterwards, contact support.
entries.quote: If a paper jam is happening, remove the paper that is causing the jam after turning off the power, and move the movable part to the home position by referring to Cutter Lock.

entries.title: TSP143IV LED: abnormal power supply voltage detection error
steps: Turn the printer off and on.
Try a different electrical outlet and turn it on again.
If the same error returns, contact support.
entries.quote: Try changing the location for the electrical outlet and turn on the power again.

entries.title: TSP143IV LED: printer head thermistor error
steps: Turn the printer off and on.
If the same error returns, contact support; the head's temperature sensor has a fault.
entries.quote: An abnormality has been detected for the printer head thermistor (temperature sensor).

entries.title: TSP143IV LED: Flash ROM access error
steps: Turn the printer off and on.
If the same error returns, contact support.
entries.quote: An access error has been detected on the FLASH.

entries.title: TSP143IV LED: EEPROM access error
steps: Turn the printer off and on.
If the same error returns, contact support.
entries.quote: An access error has been detected on the EEPROM.

entries.title: TSP143IV LED: RAM access error
steps: Turn the printer off and on.
If the same error returns, contact support.
entries.quote: An access error has been detected on the RAM.

entries.title: TSP143IV LED: FW rewrite error
steps: An error was found in firmware data during or after a firmware update.
Turn the printer off and on.
If the same error returns, contact support.
entries.quote: During FW rewrite, an error was detected in the received FW data.

entries.title: TSP143IV LED: any other error pattern
steps: Turn the printer off and then on again.
If the same error shows after that, the printer may be faulty: contact support.
entries.quote: If an error other than the above is displayed, try turning the power off and then on again.

entries.title: TSP143IV LED: Ethernet link down (physically disconnected)
steps: The printer and the router or hub are disconnected.
Check the LAN cable is correctly connected.
entries.quote: The printer and the destination network device such as a router or hub was disconnected.

entries.title: TSP143IV LED: Ethernet link down (IP address cannot be obtained)
steps: If a DHCP server is used, check it is working.
If no DHCP server is used, set a suitable IP address on the printer.
entries.quote: If a DHCP server is not used, set an appropriate IP address.

entries.title: TSP143IV LED: wireless LAN link down (physically disconnected)
steps: The printer lost its connection to the network.
Check the router settings, the network and the signal strength.
entries.quote: Check the router settings, destination network environment, or signal strength.

entries.title: TSP143IV LED: wireless LAN link down (IP address cannot be obtained)
steps: Check the DHCP server is working.
Check the network and the signal strength.
entries.quote: Check the DHCP server operation, destination network environment, or signal strength.

entries.title: TSP143IV LED: Bluetooth not connected
steps: The printer is not connected by Bluetooth.
With an iPad or iPhone this means no iOS device is connected: connect the tablet by Bluetooth again.
entries.quote: Not connected to any iOS host device.

entries.title: TSP143IV: clear a paper jam
steps: Do not pull the paper by force.
Press the power switch on the back to turn the printer off.
Push the opening lever and open the printer cover.
Remove all the jammed paper, leaving no scraps in the roll holder or the paper exit.
Load the paper again.
If the paper cannot be removed without force, contact support.
entries.quote: Remove all, making sure paper fragments do not remain. Not removing all may cause paper jam.

entries.title: TSP143IV: prevent paper jams
steps: If the paper is wound loosely, wind it tight on the roll before loading.
Pull the paper end out in a straight line when loading.
Do not touch the paper while it prints, comes out or before it is cut.
Do not let printed paper pile up at the exit.
entries.quote: If the paper has been wound loosely around the roll, carefully wind the paper tightly around the paper roll before setting it in the printer.

entries.title: TSP143IV: printer cover will not open (cutter locked)
steps: A paper jam has probably locked the cutter; do not force the cover or pull the paper.
Turn the printer off and back on; this releases the lock automatically.
If it does not, follow the manual cutter release steps.
entries.quote: First turn off the power and then turn the power back on again which will automatically release the lock.

entries.title: TSP143IV: release a locked cutter by hand
steps: Turn the printer off with the power switch on the back; never open the front cover with the power on and do not touch the cutter blade.
Remove the front cover.
Remove the paper jammed inside the front cover.
Rotate the knob on the front of the cutter to move the movable part to its home position.
Remove the paper jammed inside the printer.
Attach the front cover.
Load the paper and turn the power on.
entries.quote: Rotate the knob located on the front of the cutter and move the movable part to the home position

entries.title: TSP143IV: what to have ready before calling for support
steps: Model name, from the label on the printer.
Serial number, a 16-digit number on the same label.
The device, operating system version and software being used.
Details of the trouble.
entries.quote: Types of device, operating system (version) and software being used

entries.title: TSP143IV: load a paper roll
steps: Turn the power on so the printer feeds and cuts the paper automatically.
Push the opening lever and open the printer cover.
Remove the old paper core.
Place the roll in the direction shown on the printer, wound tight.
Pull the end of the paper straight out and close the cover by pushing both sides.
Loading is finished when the paper is cut automatically; remove the cut piece.
entries.quote: Pull the end of the paper straight out, sandwich the paper and close the printer cover

entries.title: TSP143IV: paper roll size
steps: Paper width 79.5 mm, or 57.5 mm when the supplied paper roll guide is fitted.
Maximum roll diameter 83 mm.
Do not use rolls where the paper is glued to the core.
entries.quote: Do not glue the paper roll and axial wrapper.

entries.title: TSP143IV: run a self-print (test print)
steps: Load paper first.
Turn the power on with the switch on the back.
Push the opening lever and open the printer cover.
Press the FEED button until the POWER LED starts flashing blue, then release it.
Close the cover; the printer resets and prints the self-print.
Remove the printed paper.
entries.quote: Press the [FEED] button until the POWER LED begins flashing blue , and then release it.
entries.note: Our sheet describes holding FEED while powering on; Star's TSP100IV manual gives this cover-open method instead.

entries.title: TSP143IV: turn the printer on and off
steps: Press the power switch on the back of the printer.
When it is on and ready the Power LED is blue.
After turning off, wait until the LED has gone out before turning on again.
entries.quote: Confirm that the LED lamp has turned off before turning the power on again.

entries.title: TSP143IV: use the Star app to diagnose a Wi-Fi problem
steps: Turn the printer on.
On the phone or tablet turn on Bluetooth and location services.
Open Star Quick Setup Utility and go to Printer Operation Check, then Wireless LAN Troubleshoot.
Select TSP143IV-UEWB.
Hold the phone close to the printer's LED.
Follow the problem description and actions the app shows.
entries.quote: Start Star Quick Setup Utility and open [Printer Operation Check] - [Wireless LAN Troubleshoot].

entries.title: TSP143IV: initialize (reset) the communication settings
steps: Do not turn the printer off during this procedure.
Turn the power on and open the printer cover.
Press FEED until the blue Power LED starts flashing, then release.
Press FEED again until the LEDs flash together, then release.
On the wireless model, press FEED again until the flashing changes to choose network, Bluetooth or both.
Close the cover; the printer resets and prints its communication settings.
entries.quote: When the cover is closed, the printer communication settings will be initialized.

entries.title: TSP143IV: after resetting Bluetooth, remove the printer from the tablet and pair again
steps: On the tablet open Bluetooth settings.
Select the printer name (TSP100IV-XXXXX) and choose Forget This Device (iOS), Forget (Android) or Remove Device (Windows).
Restart the tablet.
Turn the printer off and on, then pair it with the tablet again.
entries.quote: When the Bluetooth settings of the printer are initialized, the connection settings for the printer on the host device side also become unavailable.

entries.title: TSP143IV: what a Bluetooth reset clears
steps: Device name.
iOS port name.
New pairing permission setting.
Auto connection setting.
Pairing information.
entries.quote: When the Bluetooth settings are initialized, the following items will be restored to their initial settings.

entries.title: TSP143IV: cash drawer and mC-Sound speaker cannot share one printer
steps: The melody speaker and the cash drawer use the same DK port.
Only one of them can be connected to a printer.
entries.quote: mC-Sound and Cash Drawer use the same insertion slot (DK port), so they cannot be used together in one printer.

entries.title: TSP143IV: connect a cash drawer
steps: Turn the printer off and pull the power plug out of the outlet.
Plug the drawer's modular jack into the external device drive connector on the back of the printer.
The cable is not supplied with the printer; use the one that came with the drawer or buy one.
Never plug a telephone line into this connector; it makes the printer malfunction.
entries.quote: Do not connect a telephone line to the external device drive connector as it will cause the printer to malfunction.

entries.title: TSP143IV: a USB barcode reader or customer display on the printer needs app support
steps: Barcode readers and customer displays on the printer's USB-A port only work if the point-of-sale app supports them.
Check with the app provider.
entries.quote: Available only if your application (or system) supports barcode reader and customer display.

entries.title: TSP143IV: clean the thermal head, roller and paper holder
steps: Turn the power off and unplug the printer.
Open the printer cover.
Do not clean the head straight after printing while it is hot.
Wipe the thermal head with a cotton swab moistened with alcohol (ethanol or isopropyl alcohol) to remove blackened paper dust.
Wipe the rubber roller with a soft dry cloth, turning it to clean all the way round.
Remove dust and paper particles from the paper holder; do not blow air into it.
Turn the power on only after the alcohol has completely dried.
entries.quote: Put an alcohol solvent (ethanol, isopropyl alcohol) on a cotton swab and wipe the thermal area of the head.

entries.title: TSP143IV: clean the outside of the printer
steps: Turn the power off and unplug the printer.
Wipe the plastic with a soft, dry, clean cloth.
If very dirty, use a well-wrung cloth dampened with water and a very small amount of neutral detergent, then wipe dry.
Never use undiluted detergent.
entries.quote: Do not use neutral detergent without diluting it.

entries.title: TSP143IV: find the printer's Bluetooth name
steps: Run a self-print.
Read Dev Name under Bluetooth Information on the printout.
The default name looks like TSP100IV-XXXXX.
entries.quote: can be checked via [Dev Name] of ***Bluetooth Information*** printed via Self-Printing

entries.title: TSP143IV: pair with an iPad or iPhone by Bluetooth
steps: Turn the printer on.
On the tablet open Settings, then Bluetooth, and turn Bluetooth on.
Select the printer name (TSP100IV-XXXXX).
When it is connected, "Connected" shows next to the name.
entries.quote: When connection is completed, "Connected" will be displayed next to the device name.

entries.title: TSP143IV: pair with an Android tablet by Bluetooth
steps: Turn the printer on and turn Bluetooth on on the tablet.
Open Settings, then Connected devices, then Pair new device.
Select the printer name (TSP100IV-XXXXX).
When pairing is complete the name shows under Saved devices.
entries.quote: Once pairing is complete, the device name will be displayed under "Saved devices".

entries.title: TSP143IV on Windows: "Driver is unavailable" after Bluetooth pairing
steps: This message appears after a while and can be ignored.
Pairing is already complete.
entries.quote: After a while, "Driver is unavailable" will be displayed, however, pairing is completed.

entries.title: TSP143IV: tablet was "forgotten" while New Pairing Permission was OFF
steps: With New Pairing Permission OFF, the printer will not pair again, even with the same tablet.
Initialize the printer's communication settings.
Pair the tablet again.
entries.quote: If you accidentally delete the device, then perform Initialize Communication Settings, and re-pair the tablet.

entries.title: TSP143IV: wireless setup QR codes do not print
steps: The QR codes do not print if Wi-Fi is already set up, if a USB or LAN cable is connected, or if Bluetooth was paired before.
Initialize the communication settings.
Turn the printer on again; the two QR codes print about 20 seconds after power-on.
entries.quote: The QR codes for wireless communication setting are not printed when the wireless LAN settings are already configured

entries.title: TSP143IV: connect to Wi-Fi with the Star Quick Setup Utility app
steps: Turn the printer on; on the phone turn on Bluetooth and location services.
Open Star Quick Setup Utility, then Start Guide (Initial Settings), then Use Wireless LAN.
Select TSP143IV-UEWB and allow the permissions it asks for.
Enter the network name (SSID) and security key.
Hold the phone close to the printer's LED and keep it there; do not turn the printer off.
The printer prints a Wireless Network Diagnosis; "Successful" with an IP address means it is connected.
entries.quote: When the printer is successfully connected to the network, "Successful" is printed on the diagnosis result.

entries.title: TSP143IV Web Configuration login
steps: Open the printer's IP address in a web browser and choose Login.
The username is root and the default password is public.
On first login with the default password the printer makes you set a new one; after that use the changed password.
entries.quote: If you want to change the printer settings, the default password has to be changed.

entries.title: TSP143IV: set a static IP address from the printer's settings page
steps: Run a self-print and read the IP Address under Current IP Parameters Status.
On a device on the same network, type that address into a web browser.
Log in.
Open IP Parameters, select Static, enter the IP address and subnet mask and tap Submit.
Ask whoever manages the network which address and subnet mask to use.
entries.quote: Once a static IP address is assigned, the IP address will not be changed by the DHCP server, so the specified printer can be used continuously.

entries.title: TSP143IV: connect the LAN cable
steps: Plug one end of the LAN cable into the hub or router.
Plug the other end into the printer's LAN connector.
If the supplied 1 m cable is too short, use a category 5 or higher LAN cable.
Do not connect the LAN cable if the printer is to use Wi-Fi.
entries.quote: please prepare a LAN cable that is compatible with category 5 or higher

entries.title: TSP143IV: connect an Android tablet by USB
steps: Start the Android device.
Connect the supplied USB cable (A to C) to the printer's USB-A port (Android USB-A) and to the tablet.
Then turn the printer on.
The tablet is also charged (1.5 A at most) while connected.
entries.quote: start the Android device, connect the USB cable to the printer, and then turn ON the printer power

entries.title: Star SP700: paper end error (POWER lamp on, ERROR lamp flashing 1 second on / 1 second off, 4 short beeps twice)
steps: The paper has run out.
Load a new paper roll.
Close the printer cover; the printer recovers by itself.
entries.quote: Automatically recovered by loading a new paper roll, then closing the printer cover.

entries.title: Star SP700: printer cover open error (POWER lamp on, ERROR lamp on, beep)
steps: Close the printer cover; the printer recovers by itself.
entries.quote: Automatically recovered by closing the printer cover.

entries.title: Star SP700: front cover open error (POWER lamp flashing 0.5 second on / 0.5 second off, ERROR lamp on, beep)
steps: Close the front cover (the cover over the ribbon); the printer recovers by itself.
entries.quote: Automatically recovered by closing the front cover.

entries.title: Star SP700: head high temperature detection (POWER lamp flashing 1 second on / 1 second off, ERROR lamp off)
steps: Wait; the printer recovers by itself after the print head has cooled.
This is not a fault.
entries.quote: A print head temperature error is not abnormal.

entries.title: Star SP700: board high temperature detection (POWER lamp flashing 2 seconds on / 2 seconds off, ERROR lamp off)
steps: Wait; the printer recovers by itself after the board has cooled.
entries.quote: Automatically the printer is recovered after the board has cooled.

entries.title: Star SP700: cutter error (POWER lamp on, ERROR lamp flashing very fast, 3 short beeps)
steps: Turn the power off.
If paper is jammed, clear it.
Turn the power on; the printer recovers if the cutter returns to its home position.
If the cutter does not return home or does not make its first movement, it cannot be recovered: contact support.
entries.quote: If the paper is jammed, turn the power OFF, clear the jammed paper, then turn the power ON.

entries.title: Star SP700: mechanical error other than cutter (POWER lamp on, ERROR lamp flashing 0.25 second on / 0.25 second off, 2 short beeps)
steps: Turn the power off.
Clear the jammed paper or fix whatever else is wrong.
Turn the power on; the printer recovers if the carriage returns to its home position.
entries.quote: Turn the power OFF, clear the jammed paper or remedy another problem and then turn the power ON.

entries.title: Star SP700: black mark detection error (POWER lamp on, ERROR lamp flashing 0.5 second on / 0.5 second off, 3 short beeps)
steps: If paper is jammed, clear it and change the roll if needed.
If the paper is the wrong format, change to a roll with the correct black mark.
entries.quote: Change the paper roll and use a paper roll with the correct black mark.

entries.title: Star SP700 Ethernet: POWER and ERROR lamps flash together at 2-second intervals (physical link disconnection)
steps: The Ethernet cable was not connected when the printer was turned on.
Connect the Ethernet cable from the hub or PC to the printer.
Then turn the printer on.
entries.quote: Be sure to connect the Ethernet cable from a PC or hub to the printer, and then turn the printer on.

entries.title: Star SP700 Ethernet: POWER and ERROR lamps flash together at 0.125-second intervals (IP address lost)
steps: Set the correct IP address on the printer.
Restart the printer.
entries.quote: Set the correct IP address and restart the printer.

entries.title: Star SP700: flash memory write error (POWER lamp off, ERROR lamp flashing 1 second on / 1 second off)
steps: Turn the power off, wait at least 10 seconds and turn it back on.
If the error is still shown, the printer needs repair.
entries.quote: If a non-recoverable error occurs, turn the power OFF, wait at least 10 seconds, and turn the power back ON.

entries.title: Star SP700: thermistor failure error (POWER lamp off, ERROR lamp flashing 0.25 second on / 0.25 second off, 2 short beeps)
steps: Turn the power off, wait at least 10 seconds and turn it back on.
If the error is still shown, the printer needs repair.
entries.quote: Thermistor failure error

entries.title: Star SP700: power supply error (POWER lamp off, ERROR lamp flashing 2 seconds on / 2 seconds off)
steps: Turn the power off, wait at least 10 seconds and turn it back on.
If the error is still shown, the printer needs repair.
entries.quote: If the non-recoverable error continues to be indicated, consult a dealer for repairs.

entries.title: Star SP700: CPU error (POWER lamp off, ERROR lamp on, one long beep)
steps: Turn the power off, wait at least 10 seconds and turn it back on.
If the error is still shown, the printer needs repair.
entries.quote: CPU error Off On One long beep

entries.title: Star SP700: RAM R/W error (POWER lamp off, ERROR lamp on, no beep)
steps: Turn the power off, wait at least 10 seconds and turn it back on.
If the error is still shown, the printer needs repair.
entries.quote: (2 sec.) RAM R/W error Off On None

entries.title: Star SP700: load or replace the ribbon cartridge
steps: Turn the printer off.
Open the front cover by holding the finger grips at both ends and lifting.
Do not touch the print head just after printing, and do not touch the cutter blade.
Place the ribbon cartridge in the direction shown and press it down; if it does not seat, press it down while turning the ribbon feed knob in the direction of the arrow.
Turn the ribbon feed knob in the direction of the arrow to take up slack.
Close the front cover.
entries.quote: If loading of the ribbon cartridge is not satisfactory, press down the cartridge while rotating the ribbon feed knob in the direction of the arrow.

entries.title: Star SP700 (rewinder model SP717R/747R): load a two-ply paper roll
steps: Pull the cover open lever towards you to open the printer cover.
Load the roll in the direction shown and pull about 30 cm of paper towards you.
Pull both sheets towards you and close the platen arm.
Push 3 to 4 cm of the bottom sheet through the slit in the spool, bend it over the slit and wind it twice around the spool.
Put the spool on the rewinder frame and turn the spool gear backward to take up slack.
Close the printer cover without trapping the top sheet, then cut the leading edge.
entries.quote: Push 3 to 4 cm of the leading edge of the bottom sheet through the slit in the spool.

entries.title: Star SP700 rewinder: the rewound copy has gone slack
steps: Turn the spool gear backward to take up the slack in the paper.
entries.quote: If the paper roll has slackened during use, take up the slack in the same manner.

entries.title: Star SP700: when to change the paper roll
steps: When the paper end mark appears on the paper, replace the roll before it runs out.
Use only roll paper that is not glued to the core.
entries.quote: When the paper end mark appears on the paper, replace the roll paper before it runs out.

entries.title: Star SP700: never print without paper or ribbon
steps: Do not print when the paper or the ribbon cartridge is missing; the print head can be damaged.
entries.quote: Do not attempt to print when either paper or ribbon cartridge is not located in the printer, otherwise the print head can be damaged.

entries.title: Star SP700: using 57.5 mm or 69.5 mm paper
steps: Fit the supplied roll paper guide in the groove in the printer.
The print width setting (memory switch) must also be changed; this is a technician setting.
entries.quote: The setting for memory switch 2-A and 2-B must be changed to change the print width.

entries.title: Star SP700: turn the printer on
steps: Turn on the power switch on the front of the printer.
The POWER lamp on the control panel lights.
If a switch cover hides the ON/OFF marks, unplug the power cord from the outlet to turn the printer off.
entries.quote: Turn ON the power switch located on the front of the printer.

entries.title: Star SP700: run a self-print (test print)
steps: Turn the printer on while holding the FEED switch.
Release FEED after the buzzer sounds once.
The printer prints its version number and settings.
entries.quote: The Self Printing Mode is entered by releasing the FEED switch after the buzzer sounds

entries.title: Star SP700: dots of graphics do not line up (dot alignment)
steps: This is rare and comes from mechanical parts moving out of alignment.
Turn the printer on while holding FEED and release it after the buzzer sounds twice; it prints adjustment patterns.
Find the pattern with the smallest gap and press FEED that many times (once for the first, twice for the second, and so on).
Then press and hold FEED for 2 seconds until the long buzzer sounds.
Do not turn the power off while it saves, or the adjustment and other settings are reset.
entries.quote: use the FEED switch to select the adjustment pattern from the printout with the

entries.title: Star SP700: prevent paper jams
steps: Do not touch the paper while it is coming out and before it is cut.
Pressing or pulling the paper as it comes out can cause jams, bad cuts or bad line feeds.
entries.quote: Pressing or pulling the paper during ejection may cause a paper jam, paper cutting failure or

entries.title: Star SP700: clear a paper jam
steps: Turn the power switch off.
Push the cover open lever and open the printer cover.
Remove the jammed paper without damaging the printer.
Set the paper straight and close the cover gently, pressing down on the sides, not the centre.
Turn the power on and check the ERROR light is not lit.
entries.quote: Lock the printer cover by pressing down on the sides. Do not try to close it by

entries.title: Star SP700: nothing prints while the ERROR light is on
steps: While the ERROR light is lit the printer accepts no print commands.
Make sure the printer cover is locked properly so the light goes out.
entries.quote: While the ERROR LED is lit, the printer will not accept any commands such as the

entries.title: Star SP700 (auto cutter model): cutter locked or cover will not open
steps: Turn the power switch off; working on the cutter with power on is dangerous.
Close all the covers and turn the power back on; a locked cutter normally recovers this way.
If it does not recover, the printer cover and tear bar have to be unscrewed to free the cutter: contact support.
entries.quote: Ordinarily, a locked cutter will recover automatically

entries.title: Star SP700 (auto cutter model): free a locked cutter with a screwdriver
steps: Turn the printer off first.
Open the front cover by its finger grips and remove the two screws holding the tear bar.
Close the platen arm, undo the two screws and remove the printer cover to expose the cutter.
Insert a Phillips screwdriver in the hole on the side of the cutter and turn it in the direction of the arrow to return the cutter to its normal position.
Refit the printer cover and the tear bar.
entries.quote: insert a Phillips screwdriver into the Phillips screw hole on the side

entries.title: Star SP700: connect a cash drawer
steps: Turn the printer off and unplug it, and turn the computer off.
Connect the drawer's cable to the peripheral drive connector on the back of the printer.
The printer does not come with this cable.
Never plug a telephone line into this connector; it can damage the printer.
entries.quote: Do not connect a telephone line into the peripheral drive connector. Failure to observe this may

entries.title: Star SP700: liquid, a coin or a paper clip got inside the printer
steps: Turn the printer off.
Unplug it from the outlet.
Contact support; continued use could cause a short circuit.
entries.quote: If liquids, foreign objects (coins and paper clips), and so on enter the printer, turn off the

entries.title: Star SP700: smoke, a strange smell or unusual noise
steps: Shut the printer down immediately.
Unplug it.
Contact support; do not try to repair it yourself.
entries.quote: Shut down your equipment immediately if it produces smoke, a strange odor, or unusual

entries.title: Star SP700: clean the printer
steps: Wipe the outside with a cloth barely dampened with water and a little detergent, or a little alcohol.
Do not let any liquid fall inside the printer.
entries.quote: use a cloth barely dampened with either water with a

entries.title: Star SP700: where to place the printer
steps: Use a firm, level surface without vibration.
Do not share an electrical circuit with copiers, refrigerators or other appliances that cause power spikes.
Keep it out of direct sunlight and well away from heaters.
Avoid badly ventilated, dusty or humid places.
entries.quote: Make sure that the printer is well away from heaters and other sources of extreme heat.

entries.title: Star TSP100IIILAN prints a warning message by itself
steps: The printer automatically prints a warning when it detects a network failure.
Check the LAN cable and network connection.
entries.quote: The TSP100IIILAN will automatically

entries.title: Star TSP100IIILAN settings screen login
steps: The default login name is root and the default password is public.
Star recommends changing the password before using the printer.
entries.quote: Use the login “root”, and the password “public”.

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: wired LAN uses DHCP by default
steps: The printer gets its address automatically (DHCP) by default.
To keep the same IP address, set a static IP address before use.
entries.quote: DHCP is enabled by default for the wired LAN settings.

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: find the Bluetooth device name
steps: Turn the power on while holding down the FEED button to run a test print.
Read Dev Name in the printed list.
The name looks like mC-Print3-XXXXX.
entries.quote: For test printing, turn power ON while holding down the FEED button.

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: USB-C function shown by the flashing LED colour
steps: Red flashing means data only.
Blue flashing means power supply only.
Purple flashing means power supply and data (the default).
entries.quote: You can identify USB-C function from the color of the flashing LED.

entries.title: TSP143IV: Wireless Network Diagnosis prints "Fail"
steps: "Fail" is printed next to the setting that has a problem.
Turn the printer off and then on; this resets the wireless settings to factory settings.
Enter the Wi-Fi settings again.
entries.quote: If there is a problem with any item of the settings, "Fail" is printed for the problematic item.

entries.title: TSP143IV-UEWB: which flashing LEDs select which reset
steps: Bluetooth LED off and Network LED flashing: resets wired and wireless LAN settings.
Bluetooth LED flashing and Network LED off: resets Bluetooth settings.
Both flashing: resets LAN and Bluetooth settings.
Close the printer cover when the wanted pattern is flashing; the printer restarts and prints what was reset.
entries.quote: Initializing the wired/wireless LAN and Bluetooth settings

entries.title: TSP143IV: using a USB cable that did not come with the printer
steps: A shop-bought cable or one that came with a phone or tablet may not work properly.
Test it thoroughly before relying on it.
entries.quote: with a smartphone or tablet, perform thorough operation verification.

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: power does not turn on
steps: Check the power cable and AC adapter are connected correctly and the plug is firmly in the socket.
Press the Power button and release it when the Power LED lights up.
entries.quote: To turn the power on, press the Power button. When the Power LED lights up, release the Power button.

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: Network LED is off (link down, physically disconnected)
steps: Check the LAN cable is firmly connected at the printer and at the router or hub.
If the Network LED still does not light, try a different LAN cable.
Check the router or hub is working.
entries.quote: The LAN cable may have been damaged. When the Network LED does not light up even if the LAN cable is reconnected, confirm by connecting a different LAN cable.

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: Network LED is flashing (IP address cannot be obtained)
steps: If the network uses a DHCP server (usually the router), check that it is available.
entries.quote: The Network LED is flashing.

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: stopped connecting after its network settings were changed
steps: Run "Initialize Communication Settings (Network)" on the printer once.
Check the connection again.
entries.quote: Perform "Initialize Communication Settings (Network)" once, and check the connection.

entries.title: Star mC-Print3 with SteadyLAN: tablet has no network (or will not start) after being powered off and on while connected
steps: This can happen on a network with no internet connection.
Unplug the USB cable between the printer and the tablet and plug it back in.
entries.quote: If this occurs, try disconnecting and reconnecting the USB cable that connects the printer and device.

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: settings screen says "Up to 2 devices can access at the same time. Please reload in 5 seconds."
steps: Turn on JavaScript in the web browser.
Only two devices can open the settings screen at once; wait more than 5 seconds and try again.
entries.quote: Up to 2 devices can access Web Configuration at the same time.

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: settings screen (Web Configuration) does not display correctly
steps: Open it with http:// followed by the printer's IP address, not https://.
entries.quote: Use "http://[Printer IP address]" (No SSL/TLS encryption) when opening the Web Configuration.

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: SteadyLAN cannot be used
steps: Check in the Star app that SteadyLAN is set to Enable.
Check the LAN cable is connected to the printer and the network, and the USB or Lightning cable connects the printer's USB-C port to the tablet.
Check the printer's own network connection is set up and working.
Turn Wi-Fi off on the tablet.
entries.quote: In order to create a stable wired LAN connection, set the host device [Settings] - [Wi-Fi] to "OFF".

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: tablet network is slow when using SteadyLAN
steps: With SteadyLAN on, the tablet uses the printer's wired network through the USB cable instead of Wi-Fi.
That connection is stable but only about 1 Mbps, which may be slower than Wi-Fi.
entries.quote: the communication speed is approximately 1 Mbps and may be slower than the wireless LAN

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: only the MCP31CBI model has Bluetooth
steps: The MCP31CI model does not support Bluetooth.
Check the model name of the printer.
entries.quote: Bluetooth communication is not supported when a MCP31CI model is used.

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: cannot establish Bluetooth communication
steps: Check the Power LED is on; if not, check the power cable, AC adapter and socket.
With an iPad or iPhone, the Power LED and Bluetooth LED should both be blue; if the Bluetooth LED is off, open the device's Bluetooth settings and check it is connected to the printer.
With Android and other devices the Bluetooth LED only lights while printing; check in Bluetooth settings that pairing is complete.
Check the printer is not already connected to another iPad or iPhone; if it is, remove that connection first.
entries.quote: If the LED display shows "Bluetooth not connected" (the Power LED lights up blue and the Bluetooth LED is turned off), Bluetooth connection is disabled.

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: Bluetooth drops when the iPad is plugged into the printer's USB-C port to charge
steps: One iPad or iPhone cannot be connected by Bluetooth and USB-C at the same time; the USB-C connection takes over.
To charge from the printer while printing over Bluetooth, set the printer's USB-C function to Power Supply Only first.
entries.quote: A single iOS device (iPad, iPhone, etc.) cannot be connected simultaneously via Bluetooth and USB-C.

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: a new tablet cannot find or pair with the printer (New Pairing Permission is OFF)
steps: With New Pairing Permission OFF only the already-connected tablet can use the printer.
To turn it back ON, initialize the printer's Bluetooth settings.
entries.quote: a printer search or new pairing from a device other than the connected tablet is not available due to enhanced security

entries.title: Star mC-Print3 on Windows: printer not recognised because the USB cable was connected before the driver was installed
steps: With the printer still connected, open Device Manager.
Right-click Other Device, StarMCP31(STR-001) and choose Uninstall Device.
Confirm the uninstall.
Unplug the USB cable or turn the printer off.
Install the Windows printer driver, then connect the USB cable and turn the printer on.
entries.quote: If you connect the USB cable before installing the Windows printer driver to use the Windows printer driver in a Windows device, the printer is not correctly recognized by the operating system.

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: Windows or Mac does not communicate over a USB C-to-C cable
steps: Set the printer's USB-C function to Communication Only.
entries.quote: If your device does not respond to communication with USB cable (C-C) connection, set the printer USB-C function to "Communication Only" to communicate with the device.

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: cannot establish USB communication
steps: Check the USB or Lightning cable is firmly connected to the printer and the PC, phone or tablet.
If the problem comes back, try another cable.
Check the cable is the right type for the device.
entries.quote: The USB cable or Lightning cable may have been damaged. If this error recurs after the cable is connected again, connect another cable, and check the status.

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: what the USB ports support
steps: USB-A (0.5 A) only communicates with Star's listed USB accessories; other devices only get up to 0.5 A of power.
USB-C communicates with iOS, Android, Windows, macOS and Linux devices and does not support other USB devices.
entries.quote: USB-C perform communication with iOS, Android, Windows, macOS and Linux devices. They do not support connection with other USB devices.

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: nothing prints and the Power LED is red (cover open)
steps: The printer cover is not closed securely.
Close the cover by pushing both of its sides.
entries.quote: If the printer cover is not closed securely, it causes a cover open error (the Power LED lights up red), which results in a printing failure.

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: white (blank) paper comes out
steps: The paper roll may be loaded the wrong way round.
Check the direction of the roll and reload it.
entries.quote: If a white sheet is being ejected, then it may be possible that the paper roll is set in the opposite direction.

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: faint print or frequent jams from the wrong paper
steps: This is a thermal printer and does not print on ordinary paper.
Faint print can mean the paper is out of specification or old.
Paper of the wrong width or thickness can easily cause jams.
Use paper that meets the printer's specification.
entries.quote: Additionally, when the width, thickness, or other details do not meet the required specifications, it may easily cause paper jams.

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: receipt not printing and the Power LED is blinking or not blue
steps: In standby the Power LED is solid blue and the Error LED is off.
If the Power LED is blinking, or lit or blinking in another colour, look up the LED display to find the status.
entries.quote: If the Power LED is blinking or it has lit up or is blinking in a color other than blue, refer to the LED Display and check the product status.

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: self-print works but receipts from the register do not
steps: Run a self-print.
If it prints correctly, check the app, software and printer settings.
entries.quote: When Self-Printing works correctly, check whether the app, software, and printer settings are correctly configured.

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: printer cover does not close
steps: Check the paper roll is 83 mm in diameter or smaller.
Check nothing else, such as an old paper core, is in the paper roll holder.
entries.quote: To set paper, check whether any foreign matter such as a paper core is in the paper roll holder.

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: cannot open the printer cover (cutter locked)
steps: Do not force the cover or pull on the paper.
Turn the power off and back on; this releases the lock automatically.
If the cutter is still locked, contact support.
entries.quote: If the cutter is not unlocked even after the power is turned on again, contact the seller.

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: tablet does not charge from the printer
steps: Check the printer's Power LED is on; devices only charge while the printer is on.
Check the tablet's USB or Lightning cable is firmly in the printer's USB-C port.
If it still does not charge, use the charger that came with the tablet.
entries.quote: When charging is not possible, please use the charger included with the USB device.

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: mC-Sound melody speaker does not work
steps: Check its cable is firmly in the printer's external device drive connector.
Connect it before turning the printer on; if it was connected or reconnected afterwards, turn the printer off and back on.
Check the volume is not set to Mute in the app or on the speaker's switches.
entries.quote: If mC-Sound was connected after the printer power was turned ON, mC-Sound will not operate correctly.

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: receipts are slightly curled or folded near the top
steps: The printer has a de-curl function that runs whenever paper feeds, but it cannot remove curl completely.
A receipt may be slightly folded near the top depending on how long the paper sat between receipts.
The effect varies with the paper and how much is left on the roll.
entries.quote: However, this function cannot remove curls completely.

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: cash drawer opens by itself when the printer is turned on
steps: Install Star Quick Setup Utility on an iOS or Android phone or tablet and connect to the printer.
Tap Printer Settings, then Memory Switch Settings.
Set the mode switch at the top to Bit, choose Memory Switch 7, and set Bit 1 to OFF.
Tap Apply.

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: clear a paper jam
steps: Do not pull the paper by force.
Hold the Power button for 1 second or more to turn the printer off, then turn it on again; this returns the cutter blade to its normal position if it was blocking the cover.
Pull the opening lever and open the printer cover.
Remove all the jammed paper, leaving no scraps in the roll holder or paper exit.
Load the paper again.
If the paper cannot be removed without force, contact support.
entries.quote: If the cutter blade is interfering with opening the printer cover, use the printer initialization operation when the power is turned on to return the cutter blade to its normal position.

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: prevent paper jams
steps: Wind loose paper tight before loading and pull the end out straight.
Do not touch the paper while printing or before it is cut.
Do not let printed paper pile up in front of the printer; clear it before printing.

Turn the printer off by holding the Power button for 1 second or more.

Hold down the FEED button to run the reset; the printer restarts.

entries.quote: Hold down the RESET switch until the Network LED (green) in the center of the operation panel flashes

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: switch the USB-C port between power, data or both
steps: Turn the printer on and open the printer cover.

Press and release FEED to step through: communication only, power supply only, power supply plus communication.

entries.quote: Press the FEED button until the POWER LED begins flashing red , and then release it.

entries.title: Star mC-Print3: run a self-print (test print)

entries.quote: While holding down the FEED button , press the Power button, and release it

entries.title: Star TSP100III: power does not turn on
steps: Check the power cable is properly connected to the printer.
Check the plug is not loose in the electrical outlet.
entries.quote: If the Ready LED does not turn on even when the power is turned on, it may mean that the power cable is not properly connected.

entries.title: Star TSP100IIILAN: cannot connect to network
steps: Check the Ready LED is on; if it is flashing, look up the LED display.
For "link down (physically cut)", check the LAN cable is firmly connected at the printer and the router or hub; if nothing changes, try a different LAN cable.

entries.quote: If the LED display does not change even if it is reconnected, confirm by connecting a different LAN cable.

entries.title: Star TSP100IIILAN: cannot connect after its network settings were changed
steps: Initialize the printer's network settings.
Check the connection again.
entries.quote: Initialize network settings and check connections.

entries.title: Star TSP100IIILAN: a LAN network disconnect warning is printed out

entries.title: Star TSP100IIILAN: Web Configuration says "Up to 2 devices can access at the same time. Please reload in 5 seconds."

entries.quote: Up to 2 devices can access to the Web Configuration at the same time.

entries.title: Star TSP100III: white (blank) paper comes out
steps: The paper roll may be loaded the wrong way round.
Check the direction of the roll and reload it.
entries.quote: If a white sheet is being ejected, then it may be possible that the paper roll is set in the opposite direction.

entries.title: Star TSP100III: printed words are faint
steps: This is a thermal printer and does not print on ordinary paper.
Faint print can mean the paper does not meet the specification or is old and deteriorated.

entries.quote: if there are issues such as the printed words being faint, it may be that the paper does not meet the specifications, or the paper has become old and deteriorated

steps: In standby the Ready LED is lit and the Error LED is off.

entries.quote: If the Ready LED is blinking or the Error LED is lit/blinking, refer to the LED lamp display and check the status of the product.

entries.title: Star TSP100III: printer can be heard working but no paper comes out
steps: There may be a paper jam, or the paper is wrapped around the rubber roller.
Remove the jammed paper following the paper jam steps.
entries.quote: If you can hear the printer operating but the paper is not being ejected, there is a possibility that a paper jam has occurred or the paper is being rolled onto the rubber roller.

entries.title: Star TSP100IIILAN: self-print works but receipts from the register do not
steps: If the self-print is fine, the printer may not be communicating with the tablet or PC.
Check the connection settings on the tablet or PC and that the network connection is working.
entries.quote: Check the connection setting of the host device to confirm that network connections are properly working.

entries.title: Star TSP100III: paper jams
steps: Do not touch the paper or block the outlet while the paper is coming out.
Check the paper thickness meets the printer's specification.
entries.quote: It may be that the paper thickness and such do not meet the required specifications.

entries.title: Star TSP100III: printer cover does not close
steps: Check the paper roll is 83 mm in diameter or smaller.
entries.quote: If the printer cover does not close, confirm that the diameter of the paper roll is 83 mm or smaller.

entries.title: Star TSP100III: cannot open the printer cover
steps: A paper jam has probably locked the cutter; do not force the cover or pull the paper.
Turn the power off and back on, which releases the lock automatically.
If it stays locked, follow the cutter lock release steps.

Remove the front cover.
Remove the paper jammed inside the front cover.
Rotate the cutter knob until the movable part is in its home position.

Load paper, attach the front cover and turn the power on.
entries.quote: Rotate the cutter knob and move it until the movable part is positioned in the home position

entries.title: Star TSP100IIILAN: tablet does not charge from the printer
steps: Check the Ready LED is on; charging only works while the printer is on.
Check the tablet's USB cable is in the printer's USB port (1.0A).
entries.quote: Confirm that the USB cable for the tablet is connected to the USB port (1.0A) of the main unit.

entries.title: Star TSP100IIILAN: a USB device plugged into the printer does not work
steps: The USB port on the back of this printer only supplies power.
It cannot control or talk to a USB device.
entries.quote: The USB port on the back of the printer only supports power supply.

entries.title: Star TSP100III: receipts slightly curled or folded near the top

entries.title: Star TSP100IIILAN LED: link down (physically disconnected)

steps: Check the Power LED is on; if not, check the power cable and outlet.

entries.quote: Digital scanner is on and ready to scan, or no power

entries.title: Zebra DS9308: scanner not working
steps: No power: connect the scanner to a powered host, or connect the power supply.
Scanner disabled: make sure the correct host interface cable is used.
entries.quote: Connect scanner to powered host, or connect power supply.

entries.title: Zebra DS9308: reads the barcode but data does not reach the register
steps: Scan the host parameter barcode that matches the register.
Make sure all cable connections are secure.
If a data-formatting (ADF) rule is invalid it must be re-programmed.
entries.quote: Ensure all cable connections are secure.

entries.title: Zebra DS9308: not reading a barcode
steps: Make sure the scanner is programmed to read that type of barcode.
Check the barcode is not damaged; try a test barcode of the same type.
Move the scanner closer to, or further from, the barcode.
entries.quote: Move scanner closer to, or further from barcode.

entries.title: Zebra DS9308: scanned data shows incorrectly on the register
steps: Scan the host parameter barcode that matches the register.
Select the correct country and language encoding scheme.
entries.quote: Select appropriate country and language encoding scheme.

entries.title: CAS SW scale: "Err 1" on the display
steps: This is an initial zero range error: something was on the platter when the scale was turned on.
Empty the platter.
Turn the scale on again.
entries.quote: Err 1 An error of the initial zero range Set the platter empty
entries.note: Turning on again with an empty platter follows the manual's power-on instructions.

entries.title: CAS SW scale: "O-L" on the display
steps: Overload: the item is heavier than the scale's maximum.
Remove the item.
Check the scale's capacity in its specifications (SW-2: 5 lb, SW-5: 10 lb, SW-10: 20 lb, SW-20: 50 lb).
entries.quote: O-L An overload Refer to specifications

entries.title: CAS SW scale: "BAT" on the display
steps: The battery is low.
Fit new batteries; the battery compartment is on the bottom of the scale.
entries.quote: When the battery is low, display will show the "BAT" indication.

entries.title: CAS SW scale: "LObAt" on the display, then the scale shuts off
steps: The batteries were not replaced after the BAT warning.
Fit new batteries (6 D-size) in the compartment on the bottom of the scale.
entries.quote: If you use the scale without replacing the battery, display will show "LObAt" and

entries.title: CAS SW scale: turn the scale on
steps: Make sure the platter is empty.
Press the ON/OFF key.
The display shows all segments and counts up from 0 to 9; press ZERO to stop the count early.
entries.quote: Then the display will show all the segments and count up "0" to "9".

entries.title: CAS SW scale: display is not zero with nothing on the platter
steps: Press the ZERO key.
entries.quote: When the display is not zero though there is nothing on the platter, press

entries.title: CAS SW scale: what the STABLE, ZERO and NET lamps mean
steps: ZERO lamp: the scale is at zero.
NET lamp: a tare (container weight) has been entered.
STABLE lamp: the weight on the platter is stable.
entries.quote: When the weight of commodity is stable, display will show the (STABLE)

entries.title: CAS SW scale: weigh with a container (tare)
steps: Place the empty container on the platter.
Press the TARE key.
Put the product in the container; the display shows only the product's weight.
When container and product are removed, the display shows the container's weight with a minus sign.
Press TARE again to clear it; the display returns to 0.000.
entries.quote: The TARE key subtracts the weight of the container.

entries.title: CAS SW scale: change the unit of weight
steps: Press the UNIT key; the display shows "UnIt" for a second.
Keep pressing UNIT until the unit you want shows (g, kg, lb or oz).
entries.quote: Press the UNIT key until the display shows the unit that you wish to take.

entries.title: CAS SW scale: set or turn off Auto Power Off
steps: Make sure the scale is off.
While pressing the ZERO key, press the ON/OFF key; the display shows AP-10 (or the previous setting).
Press the TARE key until the setting you want shows: AP-00 keeps the scale on continuously; AP-10, AP-20 and AP-30 turn it off after 10, 20 or 30 minutes without use.
Press the ZERO key to save.
entries.quote: AP-00 This function will keep scale on continuously.

entries.title: CAS SW scale: scale switches itself off when not used
steps: Auto Power Off is set; it turns the scale off after 10, 20 or 30 minutes without use to save the battery.
Change the setting to AP-00 to keep it on.
entries.quote: If you don't operate the scale for 10 minutes, this function will turn the power OFF.

entries.title: CAS SW scale: power and warm-up
steps: Plug the scale into a proper power outlet using the proper adapter; an incorrect adapter could damage the scale.
For best performance plug it in 30 minutes before use to warm up.
Push the plug firmly into the wall outlet and never pull it out by the cord.
entries.quote: performance, plug into a power outlet 30 minutes before the usage for warm up.

entries.title: CAS SW scale: level and place the scale
steps: Place the scale on a firm surface where the temperature is steady.
Adjust the four corners until the built-in leveling indicator shows the scale is even.
Keep it away from heaters, direct sunlight and other electromagnetic devices, which can interfere with accurate reading.
entries.quote: By adjusting 4 corners of the scale, set

entries.title: CAS SW scale: keep water and humidity away
steps: Do not spill water on the scale or keep it in humid conditions; this can cause electric shock or incorrect readings.
entries.quote: Do not spill water on the scale

entries.title: CAS SW scale: moving the scale
steps: Hold the bottom of the scale when moving it, not the platter.
Avoid sudden shocks; the internal mechanism could be damaged.
entries.quote: Grab on the bottom of the scale when
