steps: Do not take the scale apart.
Contact support to arrange repair by a CAS authorized dealer.
Have the scale checked periodically by an authorized dealer for consistent, accurate readings.
entries.quote: Do not disassemble the scale.

entries.title: CAS SW scale: batteries
steps: The scale takes 6 D-size 1.5 V batteries, in the compartment on the bottom.
Battery life is about 500 hours on manganese batteries and 1000 hours on alkaline.
Take the batteries out when the scale will not be used for a long time; leaking batteries are hazardous.
entries.quote: Take the battery out when scale is not in

entries.title: Star cash drawer: first checks before troubleshooting
steps: Identify the cash drawer model.
Work out whether it is a USB drawer or a printer-driven drawer (RJ12 cable to the printer).
Check all cables are securely connected and not visibly damaged.
Note the main problem: does not open, opens partially, or is not detected.
entries.quote: Determine whether the cash drawer is a USB or printer-driven model.

entries.title: Star cash drawer (printer-driven) does not open: check the cable
steps: Star drawer cables are labelled to show which end goes to the drawer and which to the printer.
Check the cable supplied with the drawer is securely in the printer's DK port.
Unplug the cable from both the drawer and the printer, look for damage, and plug it back in fully.
Run a cash drawer test from the point-of-sale app.
entries.quote: Verify the cable supplied with the cash drawer is securely connected to the printer’s DK port.

entries.title: Star cash drawer opens from Star's own test but not from the register
steps: If the drawer opens in a test from a Star application, the printer and drawer are working.
The problem is likely the point-of-sale application or software.
Contact the point-of-sale or software provider.
entries.quote: The issue is likely with the POS application or software.

entries.title: Star cash drawer will not open electronically: use the key
steps: Use the supplied key to unlock the drawer by turning it counter-clockwise.
Pull the drawer open.
If it opens with the key but still not electronically after the cable and test steps, contact support.
entries.quote: Use the supplied key to unlock the cash drawer by turning it counter-clockwise, then pull the drawer mechanism open.

entries.title: Star cash drawer: key does not open the drawer (drawer release test)
steps: Lift the cash drawer about 2 to 4 inches (5 to 10 cm) above a flat surface.
Gently release it onto the surface; this may dislodge whatever is stopping the drawer.
Use the key to open the drawer.
If it opens, reconnect the drawer and run a cash drawer test.
If the key still does not open it, contact support.
entries.quote: Lift the cash drawer approximately 2-4 inches (5-10 cm) above a flat surface.

entries.title: Star cash drawer opens only partially
steps: Check and reseat the drawer cable at both ends and test again.
Unlock the drawer with the key (counter-clockwise) and pull it open.
Look inside with a flashlight and remove any objects or debris blocking the mechanism.
Close the drawer and open it with the key again.
If it still opens only partially, try the drawer release test (lift 2 to 4 inches and gently release), then contact support if it persists.
entries.quote: Remove any objects or debris that may be obstructing the drawer mechanism.

entries.title: Star CD3 series cash drawer: open with the manual release lever
steps: This applies to CD3 series drawers only.
Carefully tilt the drawer backward to reach the bottom rear.
Find the manual release lever near the back.
Press the lever inward until the drawer opens.
Look inside with a flashlight and remove anything blocking the mechanism.
entries.quote: On CD3 Series cash drawers, a manual release lever, located on the bottom rear of the device, can be used to manually open the drawer mechanism if it cannot be opened electronically.
entries.note: Our device is the CD4; Star's article says this lever is on CD3 series only.

entries.title: Star USB cash drawer does not open: check the DIP switches
steps: Check all DIP switches on the bottom of the drawer are in the OFF position (away from the numbers).
Check the green LED is lit, if the drawer has one.
Run a cash drawer test.
entries.quote: Verify that all DIP switches on the bottom of the cash drawer are in the OFF position (away from the numbers) and that the green LED is illuminated (if applicable).

entries.title: Star USB cash drawer does not open: check the cable and USB port
steps: Unplug and replug the USB cable at both the drawer and the register, fully inserted.
Try a different USB port on the same device.
Plug a known-working USB device into the original port to see if the port works; if not, try another port or restart the register.
If a printer is available, connect the drawer to the printer's DK port with its cable and test it there.
entries.quote: The issue is with the original USB port. No further cash drawer troubleshooting is required.

entries.title: Star cash drawer: remove or replace the till insert
steps: Disconnect the drawer cable and take out all cash.
Unlock the drawer and pull it fully open.
Grasp the till insert and lift it straight up.
Lower the replacement straight down so it sits flat and fully seated.
Make sure the key and lock are in the opened position and close the drawer.
entries.quote: Lower the till insert straight down into the drawer. Ensure the till sits flat and fully seated within the drawer compartment.

entries.title: Star cash drawer: remove and refit the metal drawer tray
steps: Unlock the drawer, pull it fully open and lift out the till insert.
Grasp the sides of the metal tray and lift until it reaches the stop on the rails.
Tilt the front down and pull the tray out of the housing.
To refit, hold the tray at a slight downward angle, line its rollers up with the rail rollers, slide it in about two inches, then lower it and push it fully in.
Check it opens and closes smoothly, refit the till insert and close the drawer.
entries.quote: Tilt the front of the drawer downward. While maintaining the downward angle, pull the drawer outward to remove it from the housing.

entries.title: Star thermal printers (TSP100 series, mC-Print): faded or light printing
steps: Three common causes: the thermal head needs cleaning, debris is keeping the head off the paper, or the paper quality is poor.
Power off the printer, open the cover and remove the paper roll.
Check the thermal head area and clear any debris.
Wipe the thermal head with a cotton swab or soft cloth moistened with 70% isopropyl alcohol and let it dry; do not clean it while hot.
Put the roll back, close the cover and turn the printer on.
Check the paper: try the roll in another working printer, try a known-good roll, or a brand-new roll from a different box.
entries.quote: Wipe the thermal head with a cotton swab or soft cloth moistened with 70% isopropyl alcohol and allow to dry.

entries.title: Star thermal printers: rule out bad paper when print is faded
steps: Test the current roll in another working printer, if there is one.
Try a known-good roll from another printer in the affected one.
Load a brand-new roll from a different box to rule out defective or heat-damaged paper.
entries.quote: Load a brand-new roll from a different box to rule out defective or heat-damaged paper.

entries.title: Star thermal printers: blank receipts
steps: Three common causes: the paper is not thermal paper, the paper is loaded incorrectly, or the thermal head is obstructed or dirty.
Scratch the paper surface with a coin or fingernail; a grey or black mark means it is thermal paper.
Check the roll is loaded the right way for the model.
Turn off the printer, remove the roll, clear loose paper or debris around the thermal head and clean the head.
If it still feeds blank paper, contact support.
entries.quote: If a gray or black mark appears where you scratched, the paper is thermal-coated and suitable for use with thermal printers.

entries.title: Star thermal printers: several feet of blank paper feed after each receipt (web-based point of sale)
steps: This is a margins and paper size setting in the web browser, not a printer fault.
The browser's margin and paper size settings need to be configured; contact point-of-sale support.
entries.quote: If your point-of-sale software is web-based and the printer feeds several feet of blank paper after a print job

entries.title: Star SP700: faded or light printing, or missing dots
steps: Power the printer off and open the front cover by the grips at both ends.
Remove the ribbon cartridge by raising the finger grips.
Reinsert it, pressing down until it clicks, with the ribbon sitting behind the print head; if it will not fit, turn the ribbon feed knob clockwise while mounting it.
Turn the ribbon feed knob clockwise to tighten any saggy ribbon and close the cover.
If prints are still faded, replace the cartridge with a new one.
entries.quote: If faded prints continue, please replace the cartridge with a new unit.

entries.title: Star SP700: ribbon does not advance
steps: Turn the ribbon feed knob clockwise and print a test.
If the ribbon does not advance, replace the cartridge.
If a new cartridge also does not advance, the ribbon spindle may be worn or broken and the printer may need repair: contact support.
entries.quote: If the ribbon does not advance, please replace the cartridge.

entries.title: Star SP700: use Star-branded ribbon cartridges
steps: Non-Star ribbon cartridges may damage the printer's ribbon spindle.
A worn or broken spindle causes light print because the ribbon stops advancing.
entries.quote: Using non-Star brand ribbon cartridges may cause damage to the ribbon spindle of the printer.

entries.title: Star TSP100 series: reset the auto-cutter (cutter error, or cover will not open or close)
steps: A power cut or paper jam can leave the cutter blade out.
First turn the power switch off and back on; this usually resets a locked cutter.
If not, power the printer off and remove the front cover.
Remove any visible jammed paper; do not touch the thermal head.
Turn the knob in front of the cutter until the blade is back in its home position, all the way towards the front of the printer.
Open the rear cover, remove any jammed paper and close it.
Refit the front cover and turn the power on.
entries.quote: Turn the knob in front of the cutter until the guillotine blade reaches the home position, all the way towards the printer’s front.

entries.title: Star thermal printers (TSP100III, TSP100IV, mC-Print3): print a self-test
steps: Make sure paper is loaded.
Power the printer off.
Press and hold the FEED button.
Power the printer on, releasing FEED only when printing begins.
The printout shows firmware version, interface, MAC address, IP address and Bluetooth name.
entries.quote: Power printer ON, only releasing the FEED button when printing begins.
entries.note: Star's TSP100IV online manual describes a different method (cover open, press FEED until the Power LED flashes); both are Star's own.

entries.title: Star SP700: print a self-test
steps: Timing is critical.
Power the printer off.
Press and hold the FEED button.
Power the printer on and release FEED immediately on hearing the first beep.
entries.quote: Power printer ON and release the FEED button immediately upon hearing the first beep.

entries.title: Star thermal printers: making print darker (print density)
steps: Clean the thermal head first; that may fix light print without changing density.
Print density can be changed in the Star printer utility or driver.
The point-of-sale software may also control density and override the printer setting; ask the point-of-sale provider.
entries.quote: Changes made using the printer driver or utility may be overridden by the POS.

entries.title: TSP143IV: when to reset the communication settings
steps: When switching from a static IP address to automatic (DHCP).
When a new network or router has been installed, or the printer is being set up on a new Wi-Fi network.
To recover from a forgotten password for the printer's network settings page.
When troubleshooting network or Bluetooth connection problems, or resetting the Bluetooth name or pairing permissions.
Keep the printer on, with paper loaded, and do not power it off during the reset.
entries.quote: Recovering a forgotten Network Utility page password

entries.title: Star TSP100III, TSP100IV, mC-Print: change the paper width setting with Star Quick Setup Utility
steps: With the printer on and connected to the phone or tablet, open the app and tap Selected Printer.
Select the printer.
Select Device Settings, then Advanced Settings or Memory Switch Settings depending on the model.
Tap Print Width, choose the width, and tap Apply.
Print a self-test to confirm.
The receipt width must also be set in the point-of-sale software.
entries.quote: It does not automatically change the width or layout of receipts or labels sent to the printer.

entries.title: Star Ethernet and Wi-Fi printers: error when no IP address arrives within 20 seconds
steps: By default the printer tries to get an IP address from the network for up to 20 seconds, then reports an error.
A setting called DHCP timeout can be disabled to extend that period; it involves DIP switches or a button sequence and is a technician task.
entries.quote: By default, the printer attempts to obtain an IP address from the network for up to 20 seconds.

entries.title: Star SP700: signs that dot alignment needs adjusting
steps: Overlapping or duplicated text.
Every other line indented.
entries.quote: Every other line indentation

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: scanner not working
steps: Check the system power.
Make sure the battery is charged.
entries.quote: Check system power; ensure battery is charged

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: reads barcodes but nothing reaches the register (not paired)
steps: The scanner may not be paired to its cradle.
Scan the pairing barcode on the cradle.
entries.quote: Digital scanner not paired to cradle

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: storing and replacing the battery
steps: For storage, keep batteries at half charge in a dry, cool place, removed from the scanner.
Batteries stored over six months may lose some quality for good.
Replace the battery when run time drops noticeably.
Use only Zebra approved batteries.
entries.quote: Replace the battery when a significant loss of run time is detected.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: pair directly with a PC, tablet or phone
steps: Scan the HID Bluetooth Classic barcode in the quick start guide.
Then find and connect the scanner from that device's Bluetooth settings.
entries.quote: To pair directly with your PC, tablet, or phone, scan HID Bluetooth Classic below.

entries.title: Clover KDS: what it is and how it mounts
steps: The Clover KDS shows orders to kitchen staff in place of paper tickets.
It supports VESA 100 mm mounts and works with countertop stands, wall mounts and other stands.
entries.quote: Clover KDS supports VESA 100mm mounts and is compatible with countertops, wall mounts, and other types of stands.

entries.title: Clover KDS: orders still reach the kitchen screen when the internet is down (Clover Local Connect)
steps: Clover devices on the same local network (Wi-Fi or wired) can talk to each other directly, so an order taken at the register still shows on the KDS without internet.
This is temporary: internet is still needed to process card payments and save sales data.
All Clover devices must be on the same local network.
entries.quote: So, if someone takes an order at the register on a Clover device, it will still show up on the Clover KDS, even without the internet.

entries.title: Clover KDS and registers: network set-up best practices
steps: Use a dedicated router for the Clover devices, connected to the internet provider's modem or gateway.
Use only one router on the Clover network; if Wi-Fi must cover a large area, add an access point, not another router.
Where possible connect Clover devices to the router with wired Ethernet; add Ethernet switches if more ports are needed.
Do not connect anything other than Clover devices to that network.
Do not let customers or guests use that network.
entries.quote: If you are using Wi-Fi and need to cover a large area, add an additional Access Point, not another router.

entries.title: Clover: the Kitchen operations report is blank
steps: The report only has data for merchants using a Kitchen Display System.
Merchants who use only a kitchen printer and have not set up a KDS see a blank report.
To read it: log in to the Clover dashboard and select Reports, then Kitchen operations, then a date range.
entries.quote: Merchants who use only the Kitchen Printer and have not configured a KDS will see a blank report.

entries.title: Valor VL300 PIN pad: connect it to a VL100
steps: Power down the VL100.
Connect the PIN pad's micro-USB cable to the USB1 or USB2 port of the VL100.
Power on the VL100.
entries.quote: Connect the micro-USB into the USB1 or USB2 port of the VL100.

entries.title: Valor VL300 PIN pad does not turn on when connected to the VL100
steps: The VL100 has to be configured to accept an external PIN pad.
Contact support to turn on External PinPad Support for the terminal in the Valor portal.
Then run a Package Download on the VL100 to apply the change.
entries.quote: If the Pin Pad does not turn on, contact your ISO to configure your VL100 to accept External Pin Pad Support

entries.title: Valor VL300 PIN pad shows "Keys Not Present"
steps: Connect an Ethernet cable to the Ethernet port on the PIN pad's Y-cable.
Power cycle the PIN pad by pressing and holding its Power button; a key (RKI) download starts.
When it completes, the Ethernet cable can be removed.
If the message stays, contact support.
entries.quote: If the Pin Pad communicates Keys Not Present follow the RKI steps below.
entries.note: Contacting support if it persists is our addition for escalation; the article ends at the download.
entries.review: routed to support by rule: steps need staff access

entries.title: Valor VP300 PIN pad: connect it to a VP100
steps: Power down the VP100.
Connect the PIN pad's RJ45 cable to the Pin Pad port of the VP100.
Power on the VP100.
If the PIN pad does not turn on, contact support: the VP100 must be configured for External PinPad Support and then run a Package Download.
entries.quote: Connect the RJ45(small phone line) into the Pin Pad port of the VP100.
